claims.head: Turnovers could swing this one
claims.call: The Maple Leafs get at least their usual 8.4% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
claims.body: The Maple Leafs turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Islanders are one of the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Islanders.
claims.nums: Toronto 1st for chances off turnovers (8.4% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · NY Islanders 31st for avoiding breakdowns
claims.gist: The Maple Leafs pounce on loose pucks, and the Islanders cough them up.

claims.head: The Maple Leafs’ power play has a target
claims.call: The Maple Leafs’ power play creates at least their usual 7.8 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Maple Leafs’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Islanders’ kill is one of the league’s worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Islanders more than most.
claims.nums: Toronto 10th for power play (7.8 expected goals per 60) · NY Islanders 30th for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Maple Leafs’ power play has a soft target in the Islanders’ kill.

claims.head: Active D against forward-led
claims.body: The Islanders are one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, at the active D end; the Maple Leafs are one of the league’s worst, at the forward-led end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.nums: Shots from defensemen: NY Islanders 3rd, Toronto 29th
claims.gist: The Islanders and the Maple Leafs sit at opposite ends for shots from defensemen.
claims.call: The Islanders’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Maple Leafs’.

notes.text: M. Barzal is day to day and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters. V. Eklund has taken his spot beside B. Schenn and C. Ritchie.
K. Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 37% last season.
J. Tavares is out and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
O. Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, up from 6% last season.

TOR.head: Close, but the Islanders have the slight edge
TOR.body: The Islanders have controlled the play far better over recent games, Toronto will be without Tavares, the Islanders may be without Barzal, and Toronto has home ice. Toronto can tip it if they pounce on loose pucks.

NYI.head: The Islanders start a half-step ahead
NYI.body: The Islanders have controlled the play far better over recent games, the Islanders may be without Barzal, Toronto will be without Tavares, and Toronto has home ice. Toronto can still swing it if they pounce on loose pucks.

story.head: Round two in Toronto
paras: The Maple Leafs won the first meeting this season, 2-1 in Toronto. The Islanders come in at 2-2-0, the Maple Leafs at 2-2-1.
